newsitem.title: USA: U.S. asks more input on labeling imported produce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. asks more input on labeling imported produce.

text.p: The U.S. Customs Service has opened a new public comment period on a proposal to require "country of origin" labels on the front panel of imported frozen foods, with comments accepted until October 17.
"By deciding to reopen the record on its proposed regulation...Customs brings new life to a 10-year-old debate," said American Alliance for Honest Labeling, a group in favor of the rule.
Customs announced the decision in the Federal Register on Tuesday.

It held a public comment period in 1996 but there has been "a large number of additional coments and other correspondence" on the matter since then, the agency said in explaining the why a new 60-day comment period was offered.
At present, imported produce is required to display the country of origin conspicuously. Critics say the information often is printed in obscure places in easily smudged ink or not provided at all.
Opponents of the front-panel rule say it may violate trade rules and would impede food processing.
